title: How Russia Is Attacking the Midterms with a Mother Jones Deepfake

reading.body:
This is an impersonation failure. A fabricated video was published under another organisation's brand, with invented quotes attributed to a named editor and invented documents attributed to a hacking group. The false claim was carried by the impersonated branding rather than by any real statement from the outlet.

The deployment point is a social platform's open posting surface. The account that posted it had no followers and no prior posts, so no reputation signal existed to weigh against the content. Detection therefore had to come from the platform's own policy enforcement or from external researchers, and the platform acted only after the impersonated outlet complained. Catching it earlier would have required either automated matching of brand assets to authorised accounts or proactive review of new accounts posting high-reach political video.

What is not established is who exactly operated the account, and the attribution to a named campaign rests on researcher identification rather than on any finding presented in the reporting.

reports.title: How Russia Is Attacking the Midterms with a Mother Jones Deepfake

summary:
A fake Mother Jones video circulated on X, falsely claiming the Democratic National Committee paid $259 million to CNN chief Mark Thompson to promote gender transition among children. The video, branded with a Mother Jones logo, featured fabricated quotes attributed to editor-in-chief Clara Jeffery and cited emails supposedly hacked by Anonymous. It was posted by an account called роман, which had no followers and no prior posts, and drew 155,000 views within a day, plus 50,000 more from another account. Researchers identified it as part of a Russian disinformation campaign called Storm-1679 or Matryoshka, which has also posted deepfakes of celebrities urging votes for Republicans.

Mother Jones complained to X, which removed the post for violating its trademark policy. The campaign has targeted the 2026 midterms, though it has not yet achieved major reach. The article notes that the Trump administration has closed FBI, intelligence, and State Department units that once tracked Russian disinformation, leaving the US less able to counter such operations.
